headword: {伝統産業|でんとうさんぎょう}

definitions.explanation: Industries rooted in historical craft techniques and local materials, typically producing goods such as pottery, textiles, lacquerware, and paper. In Japan, many are officially designated and supported by local and national government programs.

examples.japanese: {京都|きょうと}は{伝統産業|でんとうさんぎょう}の{町|まち}だ。
examples.english: Kyoto is a city of traditional industries.

examples.japanese: {伝統産業|でんとうさんぎょう}の{後継者|こうけいしゃ}{不足|ぶそく}が{問題|もんだい}になっている。
examples.english: A shortage of successors in traditional industries has become a problem.

examples.japanese: {地域|ちいき}の{伝統産業|でんとうさんぎょう}を{守|まも}るために、{若|わか}い{職人|しょくにん}の{育成|いくせい}に{力|ちから}を{入|い}れている。
examples.english: They are focusing on training young artisans to preserve the region's traditional industries.

examples.japanese: {伝統産業|でんとうさんぎょう}{会館|かいかん}では{漆器|しっき}や{織物|おりもの}の{制作|せいさく}{体験|たいけん}ができる。
examples.english: At the traditional industry center, you can try your hand at making lacquerware and textiles.

notes:
Composed of {伝統|でんとう} (tradition) and {産業|さんぎょう} (industry). Japan designates certain crafts as {伝統的工芸品|でんとうてきこうげいひん} (traditional craft products) under national law, providing support for their preservation. Major examples include {西陣織|にしじんおり} (Nishijin weaving), {有田焼|ありたやき} (Arita porcelain), and {輪島塗|わじまぬり} (Wajima lacquerware).

A recurring theme in discussions of {伝統産業|でんとうさんぎょう} is the tension between preservation and modernization, as many face declining demand and a shortage of young artisans willing to carry on the craft.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {伝統産業|でんとうさんぎょう}の{振興|しんこう}: promotion of traditional industries
- {伝統産業|でんとうさんぎょう}の{後継者|こうけいしゃ}: successors in traditional industries
- {伝統産業|でんとうさんぎょう}{会館|かいかん}: traditional industry center/hall
- {地場|じば}の{伝統産業|でんとうさんぎょう}: local traditional industry
- {伝統産業|でんとうさんぎょう}を{支|ささ}える: to support traditional industries

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {伝統工芸|でんとうこうげい}: traditional craft — focuses on the artistic/handcraft dimension rather than the industrial/economic one
- {地場産業|じばさんぎょう}: local industry — industry rooted in a specific region, not necessarily traditional
- {家内工業|かないこうぎょう}: cottage industry — small-scale production done at home or in small workshops
